evidence.head: edffdc19868b7d8d9139bc8272405a30ce28bb3d
evidence.excerpt: Outbox algorithm: domain mutation and serialized event are written in one local database transaction. A service-owned relay locks batches (FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED), publishes persistent messages with publisher confirms and only then sets published_at. Confirm/crash ambiguity creates duplicates, handled by consumers. Keep eventId stable across retries; partition/order by aggregate only where required and use revisions for stale updates. Acknowledge delivery after durable effects. TTL/retention, relay leases, retry budgets and replay tooling must be specified and tested with first handlers. M0 provides tables/design only, not working consumption or relays.

Estate Service is implemented, independently buildable and container-tested All requested acceptance checks completed locally: Java 21 build/tests, PostgreSQL startup, fresh and upgrade Flyway migrations, REST APIs, JWT authorization, atomic outbox creation, real RabbitMQ publication, Docker image and reproducible instructions

All existing non-placeholder foundation behavior was preserved, including the four security policy checks and the V1 migration The entry point was renamed from Application to EstateServiceApplication because Windows class loading confused Application.class with the application package during Hibernate startup only the BOM-managed validation starter was added Python contract verification uses the existing contracts baseline versions.

All routes use /api/v1, bearer JWTs and JSON Collections support status, page and size, stable ID ordering and SQL-scoped pagination Creation returns 201 resource commands support validation and Problem Details No physical-delete API exists.

X-Correlation-ID accepts a UUID, generates a replacement when missing/invalid, propagates into errors/events/logging and returns in response headers /v3/api-docs is generated and authenticated The pinned OpenAPI contract and runtime document validate and contain the same sixteen operations.

V1 is unchanged V2 creates estate, division, plantation_block and rubber_clone, and extends outbox_event with delivery status and retry scheduling The existing processed_event idempotency table is retained Published V1 outbox rows remain published after upgrade All tables/queries are Estate Service-owned there are no cross-service foreign keys, entities, databases or source dependencies.

Estate/clone codes are globally unique division/block codes are unique within an estate Codes normalize to uppercase Domain checks plus composite foreign keys enforce existing parents and matching estate relationships Active blocks require positive area inactive blocks permit zero All areas are nonnegative with at most four decimal places Counts are nonnegative and tappable never exceeds planted IDs and creation timestamps stay stable updates refresh timestamps and use JPA @Version plus request versions Concurrent writes and database uniqueness constraints are tested Future crop extensibility is isolated in CropType without adding crop features.

Documented decisions: divisions/blocks cannot change estate, blocks may change division within that estate parent inactivation does not cascade historical inactive clones remain referenceable future planting dates are permitted for planning Inactive blocks return false for operational eligibility downstream enforcement is documented without introducing operational transactions Clone catalog entries have only the requested fields and no update/delete endpoint.

EstateCreated, EstateUpdated, PlantationBlockCreated and PlantationBlockUpdated use self-contained v2 schemas and full entity snapshots Envelopes include eventId, eventType, eventVersion=2, occurredAt, correlationId, sourceService, estateId, entityId, blockId for blocks, dataProvenance and payload with committed revision/audit fields.

Every v1 schema/example remains unchanged V1 EstateCreated's mandatory companyId is outside the requested model v1 block update vocabulary cannot express status/tree counts V2 resolves that incompatibility explicitly Consumers must opt into agrosphere.<EventType>.v2 no fabricated company identity or implicit dual publishing occurs Snapshots are copied into service test resources for independent contract validation.

Domain writes and mandatory outbox inserts share one JPA-managed database transaction The dispatcher locks due rows with SKIP LOCKED and sends persistent mandatory messages to durable agrosphere.domain using publisher confirms Returns, nacks and exceptions retry with configurable exponential backoff exhausted events remain FAILED for operator-controlled replay Publication defaults disabled while preserving outbox records Confirmation/crash ambiguity permits duplicates with the same eventId Consumers must deduplicate consumer_name/eventId transactionally, ACK after commit and reject stale revisions No exactly-once delivery is claimed The implementation follows the [Spring AMQP confirm/return API](https://docs.spring.io/spring-amqp/reference/amqp/template.html).

Business routes are authenticated by default Nimbus validates RS256 signatures, configured issuer, lifetime and estate-service audience Trusted Keycloak-style realm_access.roles supplies PLATFORM_ADMIN, ESTATE_ADMIN, ESTATE_MANAGER and VIEWER Signed, administrator-managed estate_ids scopes reads/writes Client headers or user-editable attributes are not treated as grants PLATFORM_ADMIN alone creates estates/clones and has global scope estate admins/managers write assigned estates viewers read assigned estates Lists apply scope in SQL before counting/pagination Only health routes are public No production credentials are hardcoded See [Spring Security JWT validation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/oauth2/resource-server/jwt.html) and the service runbook.

evidence.excerpt: ## 4. GIS functionality

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: JTS validates Polygon, MultiPolygon, Point and LineString without repair. It rejects malformed/unclosed rings, self-intersections, invalid holes, empty/degenerate inputs, unsupported CRS, altitude/nonfinite/out-of-range coordinates and oversized coordinate sets. PostGIS stores 4326 geometry, provides envelope/centroid and calculates hectares with ST_Area(geometry::geography)/10000. Raw degree-based area is never used as hectares. JTS planar area is used only to detect degenerate polygons.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: Point queries use ST_Covers (including boundaries); intersection uses ST_Intersects; within returns stored geometry covered by the supplied polygon. GiST envelope prefilters bound queries. Active block overlaps are compared in geography hectares with configurable tolerance. Available polygon parents cover children; parent changes cannot strand existing child features. Per-estate row locks serialize those checks, and conditional geometryVersion updates reject concurrent overwrites. Old snapshots remain accessible through block history; no operational/tapping/latex records are read or changed.

evidence.head: 2a7dbda842141fca041510ca79481ea0454eaaf8
evidence.excerpt: GeoJSON import is a bounded JSON FeatureCollection wrapper, atomically validated/persisted in the calling request with a durable job/report. No partial features/events survive failed imports. Export preserves feature/reference identifiers, geometry versions, provenance, bbox, centroid and calculated hectares. 3D Tiles metadata is supported through layers; no renderer, client or terrain engine is implemented.

Explicit indexes: reference_estate_idx feature_active_entity_uq (partial unique WHERE ACTIVE) feature_geometry_gist feature_estate_reference_idx feature_version_geometry_gist layer_estate_idx asset_position_gist asset_estate_idx import_estate_idx outbox_due_idx retained outbox_unpublished Primary/unique indexes additionally enforce feature IDs/codes, layer/asset estate codes, reference identity and history versions Geometry checks enforce SRID/type/dimensions/validity/ranges Feature-to-reference, history-to-feature and asset-to-feature foreign keys exist only inside this database There are no Estate Service database foreign keys, queries or persistence dependencies.

Collections/export are paginated with size <=100 and stable ordering Queries require bounded bbox and limit <=100 and report truncation Errors are RFC 9457 Problem Details with UUID correlation IDs Geometry and layer revisions reject stale PUTs Inline block history is capped at 1000 versions with an explicit 422 rather than silent truncation.

JTS validates Polygon, MultiPolygon, Point and LineString without repair It rejects malformed/unclosed rings, self-intersections, invalid holes, empty/degenerate inputs, unsupported CRS, altitude/nonfinite/out-of-range coordinates and oversized coordinate sets PostGIS stores 4326 geometry, provides envelope/centroid and calculates hectares with ST_Area(geometry::geography)/10000 Raw degree-based area is never used as hectares JTS planar area is used only to detect degenerate polygons.

Point queries use ST_Covers (including boundaries) intersection uses ST_Intersects within returns stored geometry covered by the supplied polygon GiST envelope prefilters bound queries Active block overlaps are compared in geography hectares with configurable tolerance Available polygon parents cover children parent changes cannot strand existing child features Per-estate row locks serialize those checks, and conditional geometryVersion updates reject concurrent overwrites Old snapshots remain accessible through block history no operational/tapping/latex records are read or changed.

evidence.excerpt: Domain changes and outbox insert share one local transaction.
